newsitem.title: USA: NYTimes Q3 shr drops to $0.49 loss.
newsitem.headline: NYTimes Q3 shr drops to $0.49 loss.

text.p: For the nine-month period, the Newspaper Group's operating profits rose to $211.5 million from $158.5 million a year-ago. Both operating figures exclude buyouts and accounting for impairment of long-lived assets.
Revenues for the quarter increased to $557.2 million, compared with $507.3 million a year ago, and for the nine-month period they were $1.69 billion, compared to $1.57 billion a year ago.
The company attributed its higher profits to higher advertising and circulation revenues.

As a whole, the New York Times Co reported a third quarter loss of $0.49 per share, including a $0.04 per share charge for job buyouts and a $0.14 gain contingency from disposing a paper mill in the prior year.
The loss compares with a year-ago third quarter profit of $0.33 per share, which included a $0.05 per share gain from the sale of six regional newspapers, the company said.
Excluding these special factors, the company said its current third quarter and nine month results were $0.38 and $1.19 per share, compared to $0.28 and $1.01 per share for the year-ago periods.

The company said it has also completed a review of long-lived assets including small regional newspapers, certain wholesale distribution operations and a printing facility. Impairment of long-lived assets resulted in the pre-tax non-cash charge of $126.8 million, or $94.5 million after-tax.
The company said that based on its review it accelerated amortization expense for certain intangible assets but that the move should not have a material effect on future earnings per share.
